q-61714.name: Question 1
q-61714.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249141/assets/0cb01fa25e07a0f18655c9b61b732ca0738ea6fbe735422f92925a7dcc6963be.png)

What is the total surface area of the rectangular prism represented by the net above?
q-61714.worked_solution:
The surface area of our prism consists of $2$ squares (base and top) and $4$ rectangles (side faces). 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =2\times (\text{Area of the base})+4\times (\text{Area of the side}) \\  & =2\times 9+4\times 12 \\  & =18+48 \\  & =66\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-93260.name: Question 2
q-93260.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249141/assets/4ae8d09f2e4bca084d113aaa06f80570da8d628868ccd3c9c208337de303d068.png)

What is the total surface area of the triangular prism represented by the net above?
q-93260.worked_solution:
The surface area of our prism consists of $2$ triangles (base and top) and $3$ rectangles (side faces). 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =2\times (\text{Area of the base})+3\times (\text{Area of the side}) \\  & =2\times 8+3\times 30 \\  & =16+90 \\  & =106\,{\text{mm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-93343.name: Question 3
q-93343.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249141/assets/3d0b6b63883b58ecce92e395380b140b32946a4bb037e1829544539749412af9.png)

Liz deconstructs a lantern and gets the net shown above. In the figure, the areas of two of its faces are shown. What is the total surface area of the lantern?
q-93343.worked_solution:
The net shown corresponds to a triangular pyramid. The surface area of our pyramid consists of $1$ triangle (base) and $3$ triangles (side faces). 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =1\times (\text{Area of the base})+3\times (\text{Area of the side}) \\  & =1\times 5+3\times 13 \\  & =5+39 \\  & =44\,{\text{in}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

A manufacturer produces an unfair tetrahedral die from a plastic net, shown above. What is the total surface area of the die?
q-93339.worked_solution:
The net shown corresponds to a triangular pyramid. The surface area of our pyramid consists of $1$ base triangle and $3$ side triangles. 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =1\times (\text{Area of base})+3\times (\text{Area of side}) \\  & =1\times 64+3\times 78 \\  & =64+234 \\  & =298\,{\text{mm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}

q-93339.html:
Question 4
?

A manufacturer produces an unfair tetrahedral die from a plastic net, shown above. What is the total surface area of the die?

a
302mm2
b
274mm2
c
264mm2
d
298mm2
e
286mm2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The net shown corresponds to a triangular pyramid. The surface area of our pyramid consists of 1 base triangle and 3 side triangles.

Therefore, we get

Surface area=1×(Area of base)+3×(Area of side)=1×64+3×78=64+234=298mm2.

q-62107.name: Question 5
q-62107.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249141/assets/248ccfcbb3de8ab63622cfaf4c823ae1c1734742f5f8c9f14b1dfae0ff79eed2.png)

What is the surface area of the box shown above knowing that  it is $4\,\text{m}$ long, $1\,\text{m}$ wide, and $1\,\text{m}$ tall?
q-62107.worked_solution:
First, let's consider the net of our box.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249141/assets/c35bb0f7b049baa569a06532b516436afaf310e28870cfbd4790467d36e54809.png)

$$

$$

 

From the diagram, we have squares and rectangles.

The rectangles are $4\,\text{m}$ long and $1\,\text{m}$ high. So, the area of one rectangle is:

$$
\text{Area of the rectangle}=4\times 1=4\,{\text{m}}^{2}.
$$

The squares has the side equal to $1\,\text{m}.$ Hence, the area of one square is:

$$
\text{Area of the square}=1\times 1=1\,{\text{m}}^{2}.
$$

Finally, the surface area of the box consists of $4$ rectangles and $2$ squares. 

Therefore, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =4\times (\text{Area of the rectangle})+2\times (\text{Area of the square}) \\  & =4\times 4+2\times 1 \\  & =16+2 \\  & =18\,{\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Nash paints a box that has the form of a rectangular prism. What is the total area that Nash needs to paint if the box is $6\,\text{cm}$ long, $3\,\text{cm}$ wide, and $3\,\text{cm}$ tall?
q-61781.worked_solution:
First, let's consider the net of our box.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249141/assets/038c0ea6632481ee1eaece1637aac46b9a09389c0d363f4b3503b1944c039127.png)

$$

$$

From the diagram, we have squares and rectangles.

The rectangles are $6\,\text{cm}$ long and $3\,\text{cm}$ high. So, the area of one rectangle is

$$
\text{Area of the rectangle}=6\times 3=18\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.
$$

The squares have sides of length $3\,\text{cm}.$ Hence, the area of one square is

$$
\text{Area of the square}=3\times 3=9\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.
$$

Finally, the surface area of the bar consists of $4$ rectangles and $2$ squares. 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =4\times (\text{Area of the rectangle})+2\times (\text{Area of the square}) \\  & =4\times 18+2\times 9 \\  & =72+18 \\  & =90\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
